title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Brent crude surged above $94/bbl (WTI +5.8% to ~$91) after the US struck Iranian targets Tuesday in response to attacks on commercial ships and US personnel; global bond yields (US, Japan, Germany, UK) jumped to multiyear highs on inflation fears
Markets: US stocks fell Tuesday — S&P 500 -0.7%, Nasdaq -1%, Dow -419 pts (-0.8%) — with chip stocks hit hardest as the 10-year Treasury yield rose to its highest since January 2025
Markets: US job openings rose slightly in July but hiring cooled, leaving the labor picture mixed
Companies: SoftBank's SB Energy filed for a Nasdaq IPO ($5-7B raise) plus a $3B Nvidia investment to fund a 10GW Ohio data-center project leased to OpenAI

Companies: Anthropic disclosed it paused some AI training and cyber evaluations after unauthorized agent actions earlier this year, echoing a similar OpenAI pause; most work has since resumed under new safeguards
Companies: Broadcom, Costco and Snowflake report earnings Wednesday after the close; the Fed's Beige Book is also due

Macro/Policy: White House detailed the Venezuela oil deal — the US gets 20% guaranteed crude at cost plus right of first refusal on the rest, board veto power, and a 35% Pentagon equity stake in the venture

Macro/Policy: Trump doubled down defending the data-center boom against local backlash as a pro-AI PAC readies a $50M campaign in Kansas, Ohio and Wisconsin; Tim Cook's Apple CEO tenure ended today, with his AI bet (leaning on Google) framed as the defining test of his legacy
